cards.headline: Singapore’s new Primary 1 rules: Who lives around the 12 schools getting a wider catchment?
bullets: New rules mean half of P1 spots at 12 schools go to kids living further away.
Most of these schools have fewer homes nearby compared to others.
Some schools are near landed housing, parks, or the sea, reducing nearby homes.
More public housing is found within 3km of these schools than within 2km.
The changes could let kids from different backgrounds attend these popular schools.

cards.headline: Man facing charges after allegedly starting fire outside mosque in Raffles Place
bullets: A man is charged with starting a fire outside a mosque in Raffles Place by burning an undergarment.
He also faces charges for using insulting words at a church and two counts of theft.
The fire was put out by a member of the public; no one was injured.
The man will undergo a mental health assessment before his case is heard again in October.

cards.headline: New mediation task force set up in Geylang Serai to resolve neighbour disputes early
bullets: A new 15-member task force of volunteers will help Geylang Serai residents settle neighbour disputes.
The group aims to prevent small misunderstandings from becoming bigger problems.
Volunteers will offer a new way for neighbours to talk things out early.
This initiative follows a national expansion of community mediation efforts.

cards.headline: Fewer Sec 3 students taking eight or more subjects, more opting for just six
bullets: Fewer Sec 3 students in 2026 are taking eight or more subjects, dropping from 34% to 14%.
More students are now choosing six or fewer subjects, more than doubling from 12% to 29%.
This change follows new junior college admission rules starting in 2028, which will use fewer subjects.
Schools are adjusting subject offerings, with some dropping eight-subject combinations to focus on student well-being.

cards.headline: ‘Pure joy’: Singaporean serves free food in heartland every month to bring people together
bullets: A photojournalist started a monthly event serving free food to bring people together.
He has spent about $2,800 of his own money on the project since May.
The gatherings have grown from soup to include pizza, satay, and barbecue.
Community groups provide free venues and volunteers help with cooking and service.
The events aim to recreate the old kampung spirit and combat loneliness.

cards.headline: Cardiff City footballer Perry Ng receives Singapore citizenship, awaits FIFA clearance to represent Lions
bullets: Cardiff City player Perry Ng is now a Singapore citizen and can play for the Lions after FIFA approval.
Ng, who has a Singaporean grandfather, received his passport after meeting citizenship requirements.
He is the first footballer to get citizenship under the Foreign Sports Talent Scheme since 2010.
Ng has lived here, spent time with family, and trained with the national team.

cards.headline: RSAF moving to new runway as part of Paya Lebar Air Base relocation plans
bullets: The Air Force is moving to a new runway at Changi Air Base East.
This is part of the plan to move Paya Lebar Air Base starting from 2030.
The new runway will be ready for use by September 2026.
The old runway at Paya Lebar Air Base will be decommissioned.
The move will free up about 800 hectares of land for future development.

cards.headline: Singapore proposes UN framework for global AI safeguards
bullets: Singapore proposed a UN framework for global AI safety rules.
Minister Vivian Balakrishnan wants common AI rules and testing standards.
He suggested a new international body to manage AI risks.
Singapore wants humans to stay in control of AI systems.
The goal is to prevent AI from creating weapons or causing chaos.

cards.headline: Should seniors be hopping and stomping? Why explosive exercises may help prevent fractures and falls
bullets: Explosive exercises like gentle hops can improve seniors' balance, speed, and bone strength.
These exercises train the body to react faster, helping seniors catch themselves if they fall.
Plyometrics can help build bone density, especially for seniors with weaker bones.
Seniors can start with simple movements like stomping feet or stepping onto a low mat.
Improvements in balance and speed can be seen in as little as one month with regular training.

cards.headline: Singapore air quality enters unhealthy range in three regions
bullets: Western Singapore's air quality hit unhealthy levels with a PSI of 105.
Central and eastern Singapore also saw unhealthy air quality, with PSI readings of 127 and 114.
Dry weather in nearby regions like Sumatra and Borneo is causing the haze.
The risk of smoke haze affecting Singapore remains due to prevailing winds.

cards.headline: Gucci’s new ‘Made in China’ sneaker models break with Italian tradition
bullets: Gucci is now selling sneakers labelled "Made in China", breaking its Italian manufacturing tradition.
This move aims to attract price-sensitive shoppers and control costs for the luxury brand.
The new "Drip" sneaker model, made in China, costs around S$1,000.
Gucci says Italy will always be central to its brand, but used Chinese makers for specific technical needs.
Some experts worry this could hurt Gucci's high-end image and customer trust.

cards.headline: PropNex plots its next act beyond Singapore residential property
bullets: PropNex is expanding beyond homes into industrial property and capital markets.
The company has started training agents for the industrial property sector.
They expect over 2,600 industrial units to be available in 2027.

cards.headline: Australian home auction clearance rate hits 10-week low as looming rate hike threatens deeper slowdown
bullets: Australia's home auction sales dropped to a 10-week low.
Just over half of homes put up for auction were sold last week.
Fewer homes were auctioned last week compared to the week before and last year.
A possible interest rate hike by Australia's central bank is worrying buyers.

cards.headline: Manchester City found guilty of nearly all 115 Premier League charges
bullets: Manchester City was found guilty of almost all 115 Premier League rule breach charges.
The club plans to appeal the ruling.
Possible punishments include points deduction, fines, or expulsion from the league.
The charges involved false financial information and inflated sponsorship money.

cards.headline: Chery iCaur V23 review: This reveals China’s next move in the auto game
bullets: The Chery iCaur V23 electric SUV costs S$184,999 with COE and is available now.
This Chinese electric SUV looks like a retro off-roader, borrowing from old Land Cruisers and G-Wagens.
It has a rugged interior with fun button labels like "Got it" and "Travelling With You".
The V23 uses more electricity than a Tesla Model Y but can travel over 400 km on a charge.
It lacks some features like sat-nav and a frunk, but is designed for city driving.

cards.headline: M'sian student, 14, dies after being found unconscious at school hostel, police treating case as murder
bullets: A 14-year-old Malaysian student died after being found unconscious at his school hostel.
Police are treating the student's death as murder.
A 16-year-old student has been detained to help with the investigation.
The Education Ministry is reviewing the school's procedures.

cards.headline: Over 5,600 Muslim households receive S$2.2 million in cost-of-living support from MUIS
bullets: Over 5,600 Muslim families got $2.2 million to help with daily costs.
Each family received at least $120 in one-off support.
The money came from Zakat donations by the Muslim community.
This helps lower-income Muslim households manage rising expenses.

cards.headline: Strangers bumped into man at Tang Plaza underpass, found over S$155,000 in cash missing, 5 later arrested
bullets: Police arrested five people after over S$155,000 was stolen from a man at the Tang Plaza underpass.
The victim had just changed money when strangers bumped into him, and his bag was unzipped.
Police recovered most of the stolen cash, about S$152,800, on the same day.
The five suspects, all Filipino nationals, will be charged with theft.

cards.headline: This Workshop In Jalan Besar Lets You Travel Back In Time & Create DIY Cassette Tapes
bullets: You can make your own cassette tapes at a new workshop in Jalan Besar.
The Cassette Club offers a 2-hour guided workshop to create personalised mixtapes.
You can choose your cassette colour, design a label, and record songs or voice notes.
The workshop costs $89 per person and includes all materials.
Gift packaging with a portable player and earphones is available for an extra $30.

cards.headline: Tampines 1 Has A Spooky Gamified Maze This Halloween, Plus Customisable Blind Box Plushies
bullets: Tampines 1 mall has a spooky gamified maze on its rooftop from Oct 17-Nov 1.
You can also customise your own blind box plushie at the mall's Main Atrium.
Spend $150 to get four maze tickets and a free blind box plushie.
The maze is a haunted house, escape room, and horror movie experience.
